raw_response:
I’m planning it pretty much from what has worked on my land and what I can still afford. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest income here, and I’ll leave a smaller piece in cotton so I’m not depending on one crop only. The extension guy usually talks about exact rates, but in practice I still look at the field, last year’s yield, fertilizer price, and pumping cost. If I cut fertilizer too much, I worry the crop will look weak and I lose yield; if I push too much, that is cash tied up. Since some people in my family work off-farm, labor has to be simple and timed well, especially between wheat harvest and maize sowing, because that window is very tight.
